ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This is an Antarctic marine food web diagram. The killer whale (Killer whale) is located in the upper, slightly middle position of the diagram, with multiple arrows connected to it around it. The arrows in the diagram indicate energy or food relationships; according to the convention of food webs, arrows point from the organism being eaten to the predator. It can be seen that the blue whale (Blue whale) is in the upper left, and there is an arrow from the blue whale to the killer whale, indicating that the blue whale is one of the objects preyed on or affected by the killer whale. Reasoning: The question asks what would increase if killer whales decrease. If a predator decreases, the predation pressure on its prey will decrease, so the number of prey may increase. In the diagram, the blue whale has an arrow pointing to the killer whale and is the killer whale's prey, so what will increase is the blue whale.
